newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: FAIRFAX SHAREHOLDERS SAY NO TO BRIERLEY
New Zealand-based Brierley Investments has been forced to rely on the sharemarket to complete its bid for a 25 per cent stake in the John Fairfax media group.
Brierley Investments had bought 20 per cent of Fairfax, which publishes the Sydney Morning Herald, the Melbourne Age and the Australian Financial Review, from Canadian Conrad Black.
It wanted to purchase Black's remaining five per cent stake in the company, but required shareholder approval to do so.
But shareholders strongly rejected the move at an extraordinary general meeting in Sydney today, saying Brierley should make a takeover bid for the whole company.
Brierley Director, Rodney Price, says it'll now look to buy the extra shares on the stockmarket.
SUU KYI CALLS FOR MEDIA BROADCASTS AND SUPPORT
Burmese democracy leader, Aung San Suu Kyi, has called on Australians to stand up for the rights of those seeking to escape oppression.
She's also urged Australia to start international uncensored broadcasts to Burma, because of the military regime's controls over local media.
Ms Suu Kyi's husband Michael Aris read the statement from his wife while accepting an honorary doctorate of letters from Sydney's university of Technology on her behalf.
She was awarded the honour for advocating the principles of democracy and freedom.
The democracy leader was put under house arrest by the Burmese military government in 1989, only being released in 1995. Her travel is still heavily restricted.
ENROLMENTS DOWN DUE TO AUSTUDY MIX-UP
University enrolments have been badly affected by the Federal Government's Austudy bungle, which has left many prospective students thinking they can't afford to study.
That's the view of the President of the Australian Vice Chancellor's Committee, Faye Gale.
Professor Gayle, from the University of Western Australia, says some universities have found it difficult to fill quotas because so many students have decided not to enrol.
She says most universities will look favourably on students who request late enrolments due to Austudy problems.
The Government yesterday admitted the Austudy means-test was too harsh, and Austudy applications are now being reprocessed.
TOURISM DAMAGED BY COWBOY TOUR OPERATORS
Australia's tourism industry says unlicensed tour operators are threatening Australia's image in Asia.
The Tourism Council of Australia says some business practices by unlicensed operators could jeopardise the 630-million dollar market in Taiwan and South Korea.
The council says low-standard tours, late cancellations and an over-reliance on shopping commissions, have drawn complaints from Asian tourists.
The council has called on State and Federal Governments to take action against such operators to improve business practices and protect Australia's overseas image.
GROUPS WARN ON BACKLASH ON SYDNEY URBAN DEVELOPMENT
Key environment and social groups have warned Sydney will be an unliveable city if the Atate Government continues to ignore community concerns over the urban environment.
The groups, including the Total Environment Centre and the Council of Social Service, say the Government has been captured by big developers and has a "profit before people" mentality.
The Total Environment Centre's Jeff Angel says air pollution and transport are first priorities, and that proposals for the Eastern Distributor and the M-5 East will only worsen problems.
He says although Bob Carr's Government came into office with good urban environment policies, it's only taken them two years to completely destroy their credibiity.
HEADLESS BODY FOUND WEIGHTED DOWN IN NSW RIVER
A headless body has been found in Paddy's River near Marulan on the New South Wales southern tablelands.
Police from Goulburn and Bowral were called to the scene after the discovery of the body this morning.
They say it's a male corpse, which was weighted down in the river.
CHARGES DISMISSED IN CYCLONE BOBBY TRIAL
A Perth Magistrate has dismissed charges in the trial relating to the deaths of four people during Cyclone Bobby two years ago.
The company which owns the fishing vessel "Harmony", Kiwi Electrics, and director Donald Rettay, faced charges of negligence over the deaths of four crew.
"Harmony" was one of two fishing vessels which sank off the coast of Onslow after the skipper decided to stay at sea and ride out the cyclone.
Yesterday, the defence asked that the case be dismissed on the grounds there was insufficient evidence to convict Mr Rettay and Kiwi Electrics.
Today, the Magistrate said although there was no case to answer, it should in no way cheapen or diminish the deaths of the crew.
Magistrate Wheeler said without the testimony of the crew who died, there was insufficient evidence.
He said it was a harsh fact of life that "dead men tell no tales".
BACKPACKER CASE ADJOURNED UNTIL APRIL
The grounds of an appeal by convicted backpacker killer Ivan Milat is expected to be finalised in early April.
Milat's solicitor Andrew Boe today appeared in-chambers before Registrar Schell of the Court of Criminal Appeal in Sydney.
The matter has been adjourned until April 7th to enable the finalisation of the grounds of an appeal.
The former Sydney roadworker is serving a life sentence after being convicted in July of murdering seven Australian, German and British backpackers, who disappeared between 1989 and 1992.
BAKER FINCH DISQUALIFIED FROM GOLF TOURNAMENT
Ian Baker Finch has been disqualified from the Canon Challenge at Terry Hills in Sydney, for signing an incorrect score card, following his first round yesterday.
Baker-Finch says he was annoyed after shooting a 79 and admitted it was just a careless error that he had signed for a 78.
David Ecob has surged to the lead, he's five under after 8 holes today to be 7 under for the tournament, one in front of Chris Grey who is yet to tee off.
